## R Packages Used

Here are the R packages used in this website.

```{r}
#| label: R packages load
#| message: false
#| echo: false

library(sessioninfo) # R Session Information
library(medicaldata) # Data Package for Medical Datasets
library(tibble)      # Simple Data Frames
library(dplyr)       # A Grammar of Data Manipulation
library(purrr)       # Functional Programming Tools
library(reactable)   # Interactive Data Tables for R
library(gtsummary)   # Presentation-Ready Data Summary and Analytic Result Tables
library(broom)       # Convert Statistical Objects into Tidy Tibbles
library(listviewer)  # 'htmlwidget' for Interactive Views of R Lists
library(cards)       # Analysis Results Data
library(cardx)       # Extra Analysis Results Data Utilities
library(jsonlite)    # A Simple and Robust JSON Parser and Generator for R
library(derrick)     # Export 'gtsummary' Tables with 'reporter'
library(flextable)   # Functions for Tabular Reporting
library(flexlsx)     # Exporting 'flextable' to 'xlsx' Files
library(huxtable)    # Easily Create and Style Tables for LaTeX, HTML and Other Formats
library(openxlsx)    # Read, Write and Edit xlsx Files
library(openxlsx2)   # Read, Write and Edit 'xlsx' Files
# Install from https://github.com/JanMarvin/oxview
library(oxview)      # Local Canvas Preview for xlsx, docx, and pptx Files
```

```{r}
#| label: R packages used
#| message: false
#| echo: false

r_package_table <- sessioninfo::package_info()
rownames(r_package_table) <- NULL

r_package_table <- r_package_table |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    version = ifelse(
      is.na(r_package_table$loadedversion),
      r_package_table$ondiskversion,
      r_package_table$loadedversion)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data[["attached"]] == TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(
    dplyr::any_of(
      c("package", "version", "date", "source")
    )
  )

reactable::reactable(
  r_package_table,
  defaultPageSize = 5
)

```

## R Platform Information

Here are the R platform environment used in this analysis.

```{r}
#| label: R platform used
#| echo: false

get_knitr_version <- function() {

  knitr_info <- "NA"

  r_package_table <- sessioninfo::package_info(
    pkgs = c("installed")
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(.data[["package"]] == "knitr")

  if (nrow(r_package_table) == 1) {

    knitr_version <- r_package_table$loadedversion[1]
    knitr_source <- r_package_table$source[1]

    knitr_info <- paste0(
      knitr_version, " from ",
      knitr_source)
  }

  return(knitr_info)

}

r_platform_table <- suppressWarnings(sessioninfo::platform_info())
r_platform_table[["knitr"]] <- get_knitr_version()[1]

r_platform_table <- data.frame(
  setting = names(r_platform_table),
  value = unlist(r_platform_table,
                 use.names = FALSE),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


reactable::reactable(
  r_platform_table,
  defaultPageSize = 5
)
```

## Clean Obstetrics and Periodontal Therapy Dataset

We process the dataset so that we can use it to create summary tables using [`gtsummary`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/){target="_blank"}.

```{r}
#| label: clean opt data
#| code-fold: true
opt_data <- medicaldata::opt |> 
  dplyr::select(c(
    "PID", "Group",
    "Age", "Education",
    "Black", "White", "Asian", "Nat.Am", "Hisp",
    "BMI", "Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Drug.Add", "Use.Alc", "Use.Tob",
    "Prev.preg", "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth", 
    "Live.PTB", "N.living.kids",
    "Birth.outcome", "Preg.ended...37.wk", "Birthweight", "GA.at.outcome"
    )
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.factor), stringr::str_trim)
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    Group = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Group"]] == "C"  ~ "Control",
      .data[["Group"]] == "T"  ~ "Treatment"
    ) |> 
      factor(levels = c("Control", "Treatment")
    ),
    Education = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Education"]] == "LT 8 yrs"  ~ "≤8 yr",
      .data[["Education"]] == "8-12 yrs"  ~ "9-12 yr",
      .data[["Education"]] == "MT 12 yrs"  ~ "> 12 yr"
    ) |> 
      factor(levels = c("≤8 yr", "9-12 yr", "> 12 yr")
    ),  
    Hisp = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Hisp"]] == ""  ~ "No",
      .default = .data[["Hisp"]]
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c(
        "Black", "White", "Asian", "Nat.Am", "Hisp"
      ),
      .fns = \(x){
        factor(x, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
      }
    ),
    Hypertension = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Hypertension"]] == "N"  ~ "No",
      .data[["Hypertension"]] == "Y"  ~ "Yes",
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c("Diabetes", "Drug.Add", "Use.Alc", "Use.Tob"),
      .fns = \(x){
        dplyr::case_when(
          x == ""  ~ NA,
          .default = x
        )
      }
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c(
        "Hypertension", "Diabetes", 
        "Drug.Add", "Use.Alc", "Use.Tob"),
      .fns = \(x){
        factor(x, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
      }
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c("Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth",
                "Live.PTB"),
      .fns = \(x){
        dplyr::case_when(
          x == ""  ~ NA,
          .default = x
        )
      }
    ),
    have_living_child = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(.data[["N.living.kids"]]) ~ "No",
      .data[["N.living.kids"]] == 0 ~ "No",
      .data[["N.living.kids"]] %in% c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9") ~ "Yes",
      .default = "Allocation"
    ),
    previous_live_preterm_birth = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "No" ~ NA,
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & is.na(.data[["N.living.kids"]]) & is.na(.data[["Live.PTB"]]) ~ NA,
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & is.na(.data[["N.living.kids"]]) & .data[["Live.PTB"]] == "No" ~ NA,
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["N.living.kids"]] %in% c("0") & .data[["Live.PTB"]] == "No" ~ NA,
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["N.living.kids"]] %in% c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9") & .data[["Live.PTB"]] == "No" ~ "No",
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & is.na(.data[["N.living.kids"]]) & .data[["Live.PTB"]] == "Yes" ~ "Yes",
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["N.living.kids"]] %in% c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9") & .data[["Live.PTB"]] == "Yes" ~ "Yes",
      .default = "Allocation"
    ),
    Spont.ab = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "No" ~ NA,
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["Spont.ab"]] == "No" ~ "No",
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & is.na(.data[["Spont.ab"]]) ~ "No",
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["Spont.ab"]] == "Yes" ~ "Yes",
      .default = "Allocation"
    ),
    Induced.ab = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "No" ~ NA,
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["Induced.ab"]] == "No" ~ "No",
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & is.na(.data[["Induced.ab"]]) ~ "No",
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["Induced.ab"]] == "Yes" ~ "Yes",
      .default = "Allocation"
    ),
    Any.stillbirth = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "No" ~ NA,
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["Any.stillbirth"]] == "No" ~ "No",
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & is.na(.data[["Any.stillbirth"]]) ~ "No",
      .data[["Prev.preg"]] == "Yes" & .data[["Any.stillbirth"]] == "Yes" ~ "Yes",
      .default = "Allocation"
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c(
        "Prev.preg", "have_living_child", "previous_live_preterm_birth", 
        "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth"),
      .fns = \(x){
        factor(x, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
      }
    ),
    GA.at.outcome.weeks = .data[["GA.at.outcome"]] / 7,
    Preg_duration_32 = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["GA.at.outcome.weeks"]] < 32 ~ "Yes",
      .default = "No"
    ),
    Preg_duration_35 = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["GA.at.outcome.weeks"]] < 35 ~ "Yes",
      .default = "No"
    ),
    Preg_duration_37 = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["GA.at.outcome.weeks"]] < 37 ~ "Yes",
      .default = "No"
    ),
    Preg_duration_37_regression = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["GA.at.outcome.weeks"]] < 37 ~ 1,
      .default = 0
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c(
        "Preg_duration_32", "Preg_duration_35", 
        "Preg_duration_37"),
      .fns = \(x){
        factor(x, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
      }
    ),
    Birthweight_2500 = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Birthweight"]] < 2500 ~ "Yes",
      is.na(.data[["Birthweight"]]) ~ NA,
      .default = "No"
    ),
    Birthweight_2500_regression = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Birthweight"]] < 2500 ~ 1,
      is.na(.data[["Birthweight"]]) ~ NA,
      .default = 0
    ),
    Birthweight_1500 = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Birthweight"]] < 1500 ~ "Yes",
      is.na(.data[["Birthweight"]]) ~ NA,
      .default = "No"
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c(
        "Birthweight_2500", "Birthweight_1500"),
      .fns = \(x){
        factor(x, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
      }
    ),
    GA.at.outcome.weeks = .data[["GA.at.outcome"]] / 7,
    Have_Live_Birth = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Birth.outcome"]] == "Live birth" ~ "Yes",
      .default = "No"
    ),
    Preterm_32 = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Birth.outcome"]] == "Non-live birth" ~ NA,
      .data[["Birth.outcome"]] == "Live birth"  & .data[["GA.at.outcome.weeks"]] < 32 ~ "Yes",
      .default = "No"
    ),
    Preterm_35 = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Birth.outcome"]] == "Non-live birth" ~ NA,
      .data[["Birth.outcome"]] == "Live birth"  & .data[["GA.at.outcome.weeks"]] < 35 ~ "Yes",
      .default = "No"
    ),
    Preterm_37 = dplyr::case_when(
      .data[["Birth.outcome"]] == "Non-live birth" ~ NA,
      .data[["Birth.outcome"]] == "Live birth"  & .data[["GA.at.outcome.weeks"]] < 37 ~ "Yes",
      .default = "No"
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = c(
        "Have_Live_Birth", "Preterm_32", "Preterm_35", "Preterm_37"),
      .fns = \(x){
        factor(x, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
      }
    )
  )
```

Here is how it looks like.

```{r}
#| label: print processed opt data
#| code-fold: true

opt_data |> 
  reactable::reactable(
    columns = list(
      PID = reactable::colDef(
        sticky = "left"
      ),
      Group = reactable::colDef(
        sticky = "left"
      )
    ),
    filterable = TRUE,
    paginationType = "jump",
    defaultPageSize = 5,
    minRows = 5)

```

## Age, Race, and Education Summary Table

Below is the code used to create the age, race, and education summary table using [`gtsummary`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/){target="_blank"}.

```{r}
#| label: select relevant columns
opt_age_race_data <- opt_data |> 
  dplyr::select(
    c("PID", "Group", 
      "Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education")
  )

opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education"),
    by = "Group",
    label = list(
      "Age" ~ "Age - yr",
      "Hisp" ~ "Hispanic",
      "Education" ~ "Education - no. (%)"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}±{sd}",
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    digits = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 1,
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
    )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)",
    variables = c("White", "Black", "Hisp")
  ) |> 
  # Need broom R package
  gtsummary::add_p(
    pvalue_fun = gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 2)
  ) |>
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()

opt_age_race_table
```

## Extract ARD from `gtsummary`

In this section, we exploring the Analysis Ready Data (ARD) from our summary table.

```{r}
#| label: extract age race education table ard

age_race_education_ard_list <- gtsummary::gather_ard(
  opt_age_race_table
)

age_race_education_ard_list |> 
  listviewer::reactjson()
```

### Extract Education Summary ARD

We extract the education summary ARD.

```{r}
#| label: extract education summary ard

education_summary_ard <- age_race_education_ard_list |> 
  purrr::pluck("tbl_summary") |> 
  cards::apply_fmt_fun() |> 
  cards::unlist_ard_columns(
    -c("stat", "fmt_fun", "warning", "error")
  ) |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    .data[["variable"]] == "Education" &
    .data[["variable_level"]] == "≤8 yr"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: print education summary ard

education_summary_ard |> 
  reactable::reactable(
    filterable = TRUE,
    paginationType = "jump",
    defaultPageSize = 3,
    minRows = 3)
```

### Extract Education statistics ARD

We extract the education summary statistics ARD.

```{r}
#| label: extract education statistics ard

education_statistics_ard <- age_race_education_ard_list |> 
  purrr::pluck("add_p", "Education") |> 
  cards::apply_fmt_fun() |> 
  cards::unlist_ard_columns(
    -c("stat", "fmt_fun", "warning", "error")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: print education statistics ard

education_summary_ard |> 
  reactable::reactable(
    filterable = TRUE,
    paginationType = "jump",
    defaultPageSize = 1,
    minRows = 1)

```
  
### Combine and convert as Json

We combine the two ARD together and convert the data frame to json.

```{r}
#| label: extract ARD as Json

education_summary_ard <- age_race_education_ard_list |> 
  purrr::pluck("tbl_summary") |> 
  cards::apply_fmt_fun() |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    .data[["variable"]] == "Education"
  )

education_statistics_ard  <- age_race_education_ard_list |> 
  purrr::pluck("add_p", "Education") |> 
  cards::apply_fmt_fun() 

education_ard <- cards::bind_ard(
  education_summary_ard,
  education_statistics_ard
)

age_race_ard_json <- education_ard |> 
  cards::as_nested_list() |>
  jsonlite::toJSON(
    pretty = TRUE,
    auto_unbox = TRUE, # Convert ["value"] to "value"
    force = TRUE, # Convert NULL to {},
    digits = NA # Full precision
  )

age_race_ard_json |> 
  write(file = "output.json")
```

With the json file, we can paste the text into the LLM and let it generate the written results. Here is the JSON representation of the results in the table. Act as a clinician writing for a research paper and give a brief summary of the results.

## ARD without `gtsummary`

It is also possible to obtain the Analysis Ready Data (ARD) directly from the data frame instead of the `gtsummary` summary table.

### ARD from Education only

Here is how it can be done with the education (categorical) data using [`cards::ard_tabulate`](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/latest-tag/reference/ard_tabulate.html){target="_blank"} and [`cardx::ard_stats_chisq_test`](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cardx/latest-tag/reference/ard_stats_chisq_test.html){target="_blank"}.

```{r}
#| label: obtain ARD from data frame directly

education_summary_ard_from_df <- opt_age_race_data |> 
  cards::ard_tabulate(
    variables = c("Education"),
    by = "Group"
  ) |> 
  cards::update_ard_fmt_fun(
    stat_names = c("n"),
    fmt_fun = gtsummary::label_style_number(digits = 0)
  ) |> 
  cards::update_ard_fmt_fun(
    stat_names = c("p"),
    fmt_fun = gtsummary::label_style_number(digits = 1, scale = 100)
  )

education_statistics_ard_from_df <- opt_age_race_data |> 
  cardx::ard_stats_chisq_test(
    variables = c("Education"),
    by = "Group",
    correct = FALSE
  ) |> 
  cards::update_ard_fmt_fun(
    stat_names = c("statistic", "parameter"),
    fmt_fun = gtsummary::label_style_sigfig(digits = 3)
  ) |> 
  cards::update_ard_fmt_fun(
    stat_names = c("p.value"),
    fmt_fun = gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 2)
  )

combine_ard <- cards::bind_ard(
  education_summary_ard_from_df,
  education_statistics_ard_from_df
)

```

```{r}
#| label: print ARD from data frame

combine_ard |> 
  reactable::reactable(
    filterable = TRUE,
    paginationType = "jump",
    defaultPageSize = 3,
    minRows = 3)

```

We can use [`gtsummary::tbl_ard_summary`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_ard_summary.html){target="_blank"} create the summary table from ARD created. However, adding of statistical results *p* values is currently not supported.

```{r}
#| label: create education summary table from education_summary_ard_from_df
gtsummary::tbl_ard_summary(
  education_summary_ard_from_df,
  by = "Group"
)

```

### ARD from Age, Race and Education

Here is how it can be done.

  -  For Education (categorical), use [`cards::ard_tabulate`](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/latest-tag/reference/ard_tabulate.html){target="_blank"}.
  -  For Age (continuous), use [`cards::ard_summary`](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/latest-tag/reference/ard_summary.html){target="_blank"}.
  -  For White, Black, Hisp (dichotomous), use [`cards::ard_tabulate_value`](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/latest-tag/reference/ard_tabulate_value.html){target="_blank"}.

We then combine using [`cards::ard_stack`](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/latest-tag/reference/ard_stack.html){target="_blank"}.

```{r}
#| label: build cards

age_race_education_ard_from_df <- opt_age_race_data |>
  cards::ard_stack(
    cards::ard_summary(
      variables = c("Age"),
      statistic = list(
        Age = cards::continuous_summary_fns(
          summaries = c("mean", "sd")
        )
      ),
      stat_label = list(
        Age = list(mean = "Mean", sd = "SD")
      ),
      fmt_fun = list(
        Age = list(
          mean = \(x) gtsummary::style_number(x, digits = 1)
        )
      )
    ),
    cards::ard_tabulate_value(variables = c("White", "Black", "Hisp")),
    cards::ard_tabulate(variables = c("Education")),
    .by = "Group",
    .missing = TRUE,
    .attributes = TRUE,
    .total_n = TRUE
  )
```

We can use [`gtsummary::tbl_ard_summary`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_ard_summary.html){target="_blank"} create the summary table from ARD created. However, adding of statistical results *p* values is currently not supported.

```{r}
#| label: create education summary table from age_race_ard_from_df

age_race_education_ard_from_df |> 
  gtsummary::tbl_ard_summary(
    by = "Group",
    label = list(
      "Age" ~ "Age - yr",
      "Hisp" ~ "Hispanic",
      "Education" ~ "Education - no. (%)"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}±{sd}",
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    )
  )|> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)",
    variables = c("White", "Black", "Hisp")
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()


```

## Theming in `gtsummary`

```{r}
#| label: jama theming in gtsummary

gtsummary::theme_gtsummary_journal(journal = "jama")

opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education"),
    by = "Group",
    label = list(
      "Age" ~ "Age - yr",
      "Hisp" ~ "Hispanic",
      "Education" ~ "Education - no. (%)"
    )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)",
    variables = c("White", "Black", "Hisp")
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_p() 

gtsummary::reset_gtsummary_theme()
```

## Export Tables from `gtsummary`

### Exporting Tables from `gtsummary` using derrick

```{r}
#| label: export table using derrick

paths <- derrick::gtsummary_reporter(
  gts_obj = opt_age_race_table,
  file_path = "outputs/t-demog.rtf",
  output_types = c("RTF", "TXT", "DOCX", "PDF", "HTML"),
  column_widths = "3|1|1|1",
  report_orientation = "portrait",
  report_paper_size = "A4",
  max_chars_per_line = 132,
  save_rds = FALSE
)

paths
```


### Exporting Tables from `gtsummary` to Word using flextable

```{r}
#| label: export table to Word using flextable

opt_age_race_flextable <- opt_age_race_table |> 
  gtsummary::as_flex_table() |> 
  flextable::width(
    width = c(3, 1, 1, 1),
    unit = "in")
  
# Define text formatting properties (font family, size, color, etc.)
text_prop <- officer::fp_text(
  font.family = "Arial",
  font.size = 11, 
  color = "black"
)

wd_document <- officer::read_docx() |> 
  officer::body_add_fpar(
    officer::fpar(
      officer::ftext("Here is the summary table:", text_prop),
      officer::run_linebreak()
    ),
    style = "Normal"
  ) |> 
  flextable::body_add_flextable(value = opt_age_race_flextable)

print(wd_document, target = "table.docx")

if(interactive()) {
  oxview::ox_view("table.docx")
}
```

### Exporting Tables from `gtsummary` to Excel using flexlsx and openxlsx2

```{r}
#| label: export table to Excel using flextable and flexlsx

opt_age_race_flextable <- opt_age_race_table |> 
  gtsummary::as_flex_table()

# Create a workbook
wb <- openxlsx2::wb_workbook()

wb <- wb |> 
  openxlsx2::wb_add_worksheet(
    sheet = "Results"
  ) |> 
  flexlsx::wb_add_flextable(
    sheet = "Results", 
    ft = opt_age_race_flextable, 
    dims = "A1"
  ) |> 
  openxlsx2::wb_add_cell_style(
    sheet = "Results", 
    dims = openxlsx2::wb_dims(rows = c(4:6, 8:10), cols = 1), 
    indent = 1
    # style = style_indented
    # horizontal = "right"
  ) |> 
  openxlsx2::wb_set_col_widths(
    sheet = "Results", 
    cols = 1:4, 
    widths = "auto"
  ) |> 
  openxlsx2::wb_save(
    file = "table.xlsx"
  )

if(interactive()) {
  oxview::ox_view("table.xlsx")
}
```

### Exporting Tables from `gtsummary` to Excel using huxtable and openxlsx

```{r}
#| label: export table to Excel using huxtable and openxlsx

# Similar to https://www.pipinghotdata.com/posts/2024-07-26-gtsummary-to-excel/
opt_age_race_hux_table <- opt_age_race_table |> 
  gtsummary::as_hux_table()

# Create a workbook
wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()

huxtable::as_Workbook(opt_age_race_hux_table, wb, sheet = "Results")

openxlsx::addStyle(
  wb, 
  sheet = "Results", 
  style = openxlsx::createStyle(indent = 1), 
  rows = c(4:6, 8:10), 
  cols = 1, 
  gridExpand = TRUE
)

openxlsx::setColWidths(
  wb, 
  cols = 1:4,
  sheet = "Results", 
  widths = "auto"
)

openxlsx::setRowHeights(
  wb, 
  rows = 1,
  sheet = "Results", 
  heights = 30
)

openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, "table_hux_table.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)

if(interactive()) {
  oxview::ox_view("table_hux_table.xlsx")
}
```
